submitted.rationale: Index 0 (Pb 0.76) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0049%, versus 0.0027% at index 8 (Pb2Sb2O7) and 0.0020% at index 20 (Sb-rich). EQE rises toward the Pb-rich end, which fits the Pb-rich phases absorbing 2.4 eV light better than the wider-gap Sb-rich oxides (predicted gaps 2.7–2.8 eV).

rejected.reason: Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore; measured EQE 0.0027%, about half of index 0
Sb-rich region; measured EQE 0.0020%; known phases here have wide gaps

consultations.verdict: Support: Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore (Pb 0.5) is on hull per MACE with HSE gap ~2.5 eV, near the 2.4 eV photon energy; PbSb2O6 is stable but wider gap (2.69) so weaker absorption. Index 8 (Pb 0.52) sits on the Pb2Sb2O7 composition.

Mostly uninformative, with slight support. MEGNet gaps for the PbO polymorphs are spread widely (0.0 to 3.4 eV), and experimental litharge is about 1.9 eV, so the Pb-rich end probably absorbs 2.4 eV photons better than Pb2Sb2O7, which gave low EQE at index 8. Measuring index 0 tests the Pb-rich region, which is far from index 8 on the composition line.

Uninformative to mildly against. The known Sb-rich phases have HSE gaps of 2.7–2.8 eV (Sb2O3, PbSb2O6), which argues against strong absorption at 2.4 eV. The 0.01 eV gap MEGNet gives the best-matching pyrochlore polymorph is not credible. However, the XRD at index 20 includes a strong peak at Q=1.19 that no known phase matches, so the phase there is unidentified. Index 0 is already the Pb-rich endpoint, so I'm using the final merit measurement to explore the untested Sb-rich half.
